They were called "counted" (ma'dudat) because they are few. It was said that the ten days are called "known" (ma'lumat) out of eagerness to know them by reckoning, because the time of Hajj is at their end.

Muqatil said: "The known days are the days of tashriq."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "The counted and the known are one and the same."

﴿Over what He has provided for them from the cattle of livestock﴾: meaning the offerings (hada') and sacrificial animals (dahaya) of camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿So eat from them﴾: an imperative of permission, not obligation. The exegetes said: He said this because the people of jahiliyyah used to slaughter their offerings and would not eat anything from the meat of their offerings.

﴿And feed the miserable one﴾: meaning the one afflicted (zamin), the poor one who has nothing. ﴿Then let them complete their (state of) unkemptness﴾ (thumma li-yaqdu): the readers differed on these lam's. Some pronounced them with a kasrah to distinguish thumma from waw and fa', and al-Farra' did so because thumma is a separated part of speech, while waw and fa' are like part of the same word. Others pronounced them with a sukun because they are all lam of command. ﴿Their unkemptness (tafath)﴾: "tafath" means:

All the rites of Hajj, according to Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Qurazi and Mujahid said: it is the rites of Hajj, trimming the mustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and cutting the nails.

'Ikrimah: tafath is hair and nails.

Al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas: it is removing the state of ihram: shaving the head, cutting the nails, wearing clothes, and similar things. The original meaning of tafath in the language is filth. The Arabs say to a man whom they find disgusting, "How dirty you are (ma atfathaka)!" meaning, "How filthy you are! How repulsive you are!" Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

Their armpits were clean; they had not been soiled by filth,
and they had removed from themselves lice and nits.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/50.]

﴿And let them fulfill their vows﴾: Mujahid said: the vow of Hajj and of the offering, and whatever a person vows of something that is part of the Hajj.

﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: meaning the obligatory tawaf, which is the tawaf al-ifadah (the tawaf of return or visitation), performed after the 'Arafat stay, whether on the day of sacrifice or after it. The scholars differed on the meaning of "ancient" (atiq). Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: it was called ancient because Allah, glorified is He, freed it (a'taqahu) from tyrants who would reach to destroy it. No tyrant ever overpowered it, and no one was empowered over it except those who would venerate and respect it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Tubba' came intending to demolish the House. When he reached Qudayd, he was struck with paralysis. He called the rabbis, and they said: "This House has a Lord. No one who intends evil toward it is spared from being struck with harm by Him. If you want to be saved from what has befallen you, do not approach it with evil." He said: So he sent a gift to the House, a covering and leather hides, and it was the first thing to be covered. He slaughtered a thousand camels there, pardoned his people, honored them, and kept ties with them. Thus the place was called al-Matabikh (the kitchens) for the cooking of the people; his horses were excellent, so it was named Jiyad for the horses of Tubba'; and Qu'ayqi'an was named for the clatter of weapons when he came from Madinah.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: It was named so because it was never owned (lam yumlak qatt). This is also the narration of 'Ubayd from Mujahid, who said: "The House was named 'ancient' only because no one has any possession in it."

Ibn Zayd said: because it is ancient, and it is the first house placed for the people. It is said: a sword that is atiq (old) or a dinar that is atiq, meaning old. It was also said: because it is noble before Allah, glorified is He. The Arabs say: a horse that is atiq (noble).

﴿That (is so). And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah﴾, by avoiding His disobedience, ﴿it is better for him in the sight of his Lord﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: The sacred things (hurumat) are al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the Sacred House, the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred City. It was also said: they are the rites (manasik).

﴿And lawful to you are the cattle (an'am)﴾ to eat when you have slaughtered them, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ in the Qur'an, which is His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion and blood﴾ [5:3] to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [6:121]. It was also said: ﴿And lawful to you are the cattle﴾ during your state of ihram, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ concerning game, for it is forbidden during the state of ihram.

﴿So avoid the filth of idols﴾: meaning worshipping them, because all idols are filth.

﴿And avoid the speech of falsehood﴾: meaning lying and slander.

Ayman ibn Hurrayn said: The Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon and said: "O people! The false testimony has been made equal to associating partners with Allah," then he recited this verse. [5] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/178.]

Some of them said: it is the statement of the polytheists in their talbiyah: "Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns."

﴿Ḥunafa'﴾: upright, sincere, devoted to Allah. It was also said: pilgrims. ﴿Not associating anything with Him﴾. ﴿And whoever associates with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky﴾, meaning he dropped to the earth, ﴿and the birds snatch him away﴾. The words khatf and ikhtitaf mean taking something swiftly. The people of Madinah read ﴿fatakhattafuhu﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and shaddah on the ta', meaning tatakhattafuhu, and they assimilated the letters. The reading of the general readers is confirmed by His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a snatch﴾ [37:10].

﴿Or the wind carries him off to a distant place﴾: meaning far away.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The condition of the polytheist is compared to that of one who falls, in that he possesses no benefit for himself and no removal of harm on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan said: The deeds of the disbelievers are compared to this state, in that they are swept away and nullified, so they are unable to achieve anything from them.

﴿That (is so)﴾, meaning what I have mentioned of avoiding filth and falsehood and glorifying the rites of Allah, ﴿is from the piety of hearts﴾. This is the meaning and arrangement of the verse. The rites of Allah (sha'a'ir Allah) are the offerings (hady) and the camels (budn). The root is from ish'ar (marking), which is announcing them so that they may be recognized as offerings, and they are named after it. Glorifying them means deeming them great, finding them beautiful, and choosing them to be fat.

﴿For you in them﴾, meaning in the offerings, ﴿are benefits﴾. It was said: that their owner names them a budnah or hady, marks them, and garlands them, and you may benefit from their milk, wool, and fur, and ride upon their backs. ﴿Until a specified term﴾: which is that once he names it an offering and makes it obligatory, then when he does so, he has no benefit from them. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and Qatadah, and the narration of Muqsim from Ibn 'Abbas. It was also said: the meaning is that in these offerings there are benefits for you after they are brought forth and named as offerings, by riding them when you need to, and drinking their milk if you are compelled to, ﴿until a specified term﴾, meaning until they are slaughtered. This is the view of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah.

Some of them said: By the rites (sha'a'ir) he meant the manasik and the sacred sites of Makkah. The meaning of the verse: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through trade and markets, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is leaving Makkah. This is the narration of Abu Dharr from Ibn 'Abbas.

Some of them said: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through reward and recompense in performing the rites and establishing the rites of Hajj, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is the end of the days of Hajj.

﴿Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾: meaning their place of slaughter is near the Ancient House, that is, the whole land of the Haram. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year﴾ [9:28], meaning the entire Haram. Those who said the rites (sha'a'ir) mean the manasik said the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Then their place of release from their ihram is at the Ancient House﴾, that they circumambulate it with the tawaf of visitation on the day of sacrifice after completing the rites.

﴿And for every community﴾, meaning every believing congregation that preceded you, ﴿We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾. The readers differed about it. The people of Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a kasrah on the sin in both instances, as an ism (noun), like majlis and mut tali', meaning a place of sacrifice, a site of offering. The others read it with a fatha on the sin in both instances, as a masdar (verbal noun), like mudkhal and makhraj, meaning the shedding of blood and the slaughter of offerings.

﴿That they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them from the cattle of livestock﴾ at the time of their slaughter and sacrifice. The phrase "cattle of livestock" is specified because among beasts there are some that are not livestock, such as horses, mules, and donkeys. Beasts (bahaʾim) is so named because they cannot speak.

﴿Your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble (mukhbitin)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: the humble, the modest. Mujahid: those at peace with Allah, glorified is He. Al-Akhfash: the humbled. Ibn Jarir: the submissive. 'Amr ibn Aws: those who do not wrong, and if they are wronged, they do not seek retribution.

﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and those who are patient over what befalls them, and those who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. ﴿And the camels (budn)﴾, meaning the large, massive-bodied camels. It is read with both light and heavy pronunciation; its singular is budnah, like tamrah and tamr, khashabah and khashab, and bādin like fāriḥ and fārah. Budn is the large of everything, and from it comes the saying about Imru' al-Qays ibn al-Nu'man, lord of Khawarnaq and Sadir: "al-Budn," because of his bulk. One says the man became budn (bulky) when he grew large. When he became heavy and slack, it is said: badan, yubaddin tabdinan.

'Ata' and al-Suddi said: al-budn: the camels and the cows.

﴿We have made them for you among the rites of Allah﴾, meaning the markers of His religion when they are marked. ﴿For you in them is good﴾: benefit in this world, and reward in the Hereafter. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾ at the time of their slaughter. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is to say, "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, Allahumma minka wa laka."

﴿Standing in rows (sawaff)﴾: meaning standing on three legs, with their feet arranged and one of their forelegs bound, and the left foreleg tied, so the animal is slaughtered in that position.

Yala ibn 'Ata' narrated from Yahya ibn Salim, who said: "I saw Ibn 'Umar slaughtering his camel, and he said, 'Standing in rows, as Allah, glorified is He, said.' He slaughtered it while it was standing and tied, one of its forelegs bound."

Mujahid said: "Sawaff" means when its left hind leg is tied, and it stands on three legs, and it is slaughtered in that manner.

Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿sawafin﴾, which means those tied by one foreleg, and it stands on three legs and is slaughtered; it is like sawaff. Ubayy read: ﴿sawafi﴾, and likewise Mujahid and Zayd ibn Aslam with the ya', meaning pure and sincere for Allah, glorified is He, with no partner in them, as the polytheists used to do.

﴿So when they have fallen on their sides (wajabat junubuha)﴾, meaning when they fall after slaughter and their sides come to rest on the ground.

Ibn Zayd said: "When they have died." The root meaning of wujub is falling. It is said: "Wajabat al-shams" when the sun sets, and "wajaba al-fi'l" when the action that must be performed occurs.

﴿Then eat from them﴾: an imperative of permission and concession, like His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [5:2], and His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [62:10].

﴿And feed the contented (qani') and the beggar (mu'tarr)﴾. They differed about their meanings. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Layth from Mujahid, that al-qani' is the one who is content with what is given to him and satisfied with what he has, and does not ask; and al-mu'tarr is the one who passes by you and presents himself to you without asking.

'Ikrimah, Ibn Maysam, and Qatadah: al-qani' is the one who is modest, sitting in his house, and al-mu'tarr is the beggar who comes to you and asks you. This is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas. According to these interpretations, al-qani' is from qana'ah, which is contentment, modesty, and abstaining from asking.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Kalbi: al-qani' is the one who asks you, and al-mu'tarr is the one who presents himself to you and shows you his need without asking. According to this view, al-qani' is from qunu', which is asking. Al-Shammakh said:

The wealth of a man sustains him, so he becomes rich,
and his poverty is more chaste than begging.

Labid said:

My lord gave me when I was in poverty,
when he said, "Look at my need and my begging."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: al-qani' is the poor man who goes around asking, and al-mu'tarr is the visiting friend who visits to partake of the budn.

Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: al-qani' is the one who is greedy; al-mu'tarr is the one who comes for the budn, whether rich or poor.

Ibn Zayd: al-qani' is the needy one, and al-mu'tarr is the one who visits the people for their meat, and is not poor and does not have a sacrifice of his own; he comes to the people for the sake of their meat.

Al-Hasan read: ﴿wal-mu'tari﴾, which is like al-mu'tarr. It is said: 'araka and i'taraka when he comes to you seeking your favor.

﴿Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may be grateful﴾.

﴿It is not their meat that reaches Allah, nor their blood, but it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾. This is because the people of jahiliyyah, when they slaughtered the budn, would smear the walls of the Ka'bah with their blood. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿It is not their meat that reaches Allah﴾, meaning does not reach Allah, ﴿nor their blood﴾.

﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾, meaning the intention, sincerity, and what is intended for the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Ya'qub read ﴿tanal﴾ and ﴿tanaluhu﴾ with the ta', and others with the ya'.

﴿Thus﴾, meaning in this way, ﴿He has subjected them﴾, meaning the budn, ﴿to you, that you may glorify Allah for having guided you﴾ to the markers of His religion and the rites of His Hajj. This means that you say, "Allahu akbar for what He has guided us to, and al-hamdu lillah for what He has tried us with and granted us."

And command (O Muhammad) ... Meaning: We also charged Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he should proclaim (adhdhin) (i.e., inform and call out) among the people concerning the Hajj.

Ibrahim said, "O Lord, how would my voice reach (them)?" He said, "The proclamation is incumbent upon you, and the delivery is upon Me." So Ibrahim stood upon the Maqam, and it was said (he stood) on the mountain of Abu Qubays, and he called out: "O people! Your Lord has built a House, so make pilgrimage to it." Allah made that audible to those in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and to all between East and West, land and sea, those whom Allah, glorified is He, had decreed in His knowledge would perform the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection. They responded, "Here I am, O Allah, here I am."

Ibn 'Abbas said: By "the people" in this verse is meant the people of the qiblah (the Muslims). Al-Hasan claimed that the words of the Exalted, ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾, are a new statement (kalam mustanaf), and that the one commanded to this proclamation is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was ordered to do so during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

﴿They will come to you on foot﴾: the plural of rajil (one on foot), like qa'im and qiyam, and sa'im and siyam.

﴿And upon every lean camel﴾: meaning, and riding. Dhamir is the emaciated camel. The plural form ﴿they will come﴾ (ya'tina) is used because of kull (every), meaning the female camels. ﴿From every deep ravine﴾: a distant path.

I heard Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Faqih say: I heard Abu al-Qasim Bishr ibn Muhammad ibn Yasin al-Qadi say: "I saw in the tawaf an elderly man whom worship had exhausted, his color turned yellow, with a staff in his hand, circling the House while leaning on it. I approached him and began to ask him. He said to me, 'Where are you from?' I said, 'From Khurasan.' He said, 'In what region is Khurasan?' as if he did not know it. I said, 'A region of the eastern lands.' He said, 'How long do you take to cover this journey?' I said, 'Two or three months.' He said, 'Do you not perform Hajj every year, since you are neighbors of this House?' I said to him, 'And how far is it between you and this House?' He said, 'A five-year journey. I left my land when there was no white in my head or beard.' I said, 'By Allah, this is a manifest exertion, a beautiful obedience, and a true love.' He smiled in my face and recited:

Visit the one you love, even if the home is far away
and between you and him are veils and curtains.
Distance should not prevent you from visiting him,
for the lover is always a visitor to the one he desires.
[Al-'Uhud al-Muhammadiyya – al-Sha'rani: 437.]

Mujahid: trade, and what pleases Allah, glorified is He, of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' al-'Awfi, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir: pardon and forgiveness.

This is the view of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah.

Some of them said: By the rites (sha'a'ir) he meant the manasik and the sacred sites of Makkah. The meaning of the verse: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through trade and markets, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is leaving Makkah. This is the narration of Abu Dharr from Ibn 'Abbas.

Some of them said: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through reward and recompense in performing the rites and establishing the rites of Hajj, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is the end of the days of Hajj.

﴿Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾: meaning their place of slaughter is near the Ancient House, that is, the whole land of the Haram. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year﴾ [9:28], meaning the entire Haram. Those who said the rites (sha'a'ir) mean the manasik said the meaning of the verse is: ﴿Then their place of release from their ihram is at the Ancient House﴾, that they circumambulate it with the tawaf of visitation on the day of sacrifice after completing the rites.

﴿And for every community﴾, meaning every believing congregation that preceded you, ﴿We have appointed a rite (mansak)﴾. The readers differed about it. The people of Kufa, except 'Asim, read it with a kasrah on the sin in both instances, as an ism (noun), like majlis and mut tali', meaning a place of sacrifice, a site of offering. The others read it with a fatha on the sin in both instances, as a masdar (verbal noun), like mudkhal and makhraj, meaning the shedding of blood and the slaughter of offerings.

﴿That they may mention the name of Allah over what He has provided for them from the cattle of livestock﴾ at the time of their slaughter and sacrifice. The phrase "cattle of livestock" is specified because among beasts there are some that are not livestock, such as horses, mules, and donkeys. Beasts (bahaʾim) is so named because they cannot speak.

﴿Your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble (mukhbitin)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: the humble, the modest. Mujahid: those at peace with Allah, glorified is He. Al-Akhfash: the humbled. Ibn Jarir: the submissive. 'Amr ibn Aws: those who do not wrong, and if they are wronged, they do not seek retribution.

﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and those who are patient over what befalls them, and those who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. ﴿And the camels (budn)﴾, meaning the large, massive-bodied camels. It is read with both light and heavy pronunciation; its singular is budnah, like tamrah and tamr, khashabah and khashab, and bādin like fāriḥ and fārah. Budn is the large of everything, and from it comes the saying about Imru' al-Qays ibn al-Nu'man, lord of Khawarnaq and Sadir: "al-Budn," because of his bulk. One says the man became budn (bulky) when he grew large. When he became heavy and slack, it is said: badan, yubaddin tabdinan.

'Ata' and al-Suddi said: al-budn: the camels and the cows.

﴿We have made them for you among the rites of Allah﴾, meaning the markers of His religion when they are marked. ﴿For you in them is good﴾: benefit in this world, and reward in the Hereafter. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾ at the time of their slaughter. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is to say, "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, Allahumma minka wa laka."

﴿Standing in rows (sawaff)﴾: meaning standing on three legs, with their feet arranged and one of their forelegs bound, and the left foreleg tied, so the animal is slaughtered in that position.

Yala ibn 'Ata' narrated from Yahya ibn Salim, who said: "I saw Ibn 'Umar slaughtering his camel, and he said, 'Standing in rows, as Allah, glorified is He, said.' He slaughtered it while it was standing and tied, one of its forelegs bound."

Mujahid said: "Sawaff" means when its left hind leg is tied, and it stands on three legs, and it is slaughtered in that manner.

Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿sawafin﴾, which means those tied by one foreleg, and it stands on three legs and is slaughtered; it is like sawaff. Ubayy read: ﴿sawafi﴾, and likewise Mujahid and Zayd ibn Aslam with the ya', meaning pure and sincere for Allah, glorified is He, with no partner in them, as the polytheists used to do.

﴿So when they have fallen on their sides (wajabat junubuha)﴾, meaning when they fall after slaughter and their sides come to rest on the ground.

Ibn Zayd said: "When they have died." The root meaning of wujub is falling. It is said: "Wajabat al-shams" when the sun sets, and "wajaba al-fi'l" when the action that must be performed occurs.

﴿Then eat from them﴾: an imperative of permission and concession, like His saying: ﴿And when you have come out of ihram, then hunt﴾ [5:2], and His saying, glorified and exalted is He: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse in the land﴾ [62:10].

﴿And feed the contented (qani') and the beggar (mu'tarr)﴾. They differed about their meanings. Al-'Awfi narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, and Layth from Mujahid, that al-qani' is the one who is content with what is given to him and satisfied with what he has, and does not ask; and al-mu'tarr is the one who passes by you and presents himself to you without asking.

'Ikrimah, Ibn Maysam, and Qatadah: al-qani' is the one who is modest, sitting in his house, and al-mu'tarr is the beggar who comes to you and asks you. This is the narration of al-Walibi from Ibn 'Abbas. According to these interpretations, al-qani' is from qana'ah, which is contentment, modesty, and abstaining from asking.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Kalbi: al-qani' is the one who asks you, and al-mu'tarr is the one who presents himself to you and shows you his need without asking. According to this view, al-qani' is from qunu', which is asking. Al-Shammakh said:

The wealth of a man sustains him, so he becomes rich,
and his poverty is more chaste than begging.

Labid said:

My lord gave me when I was in poverty,
when he said, "Look at my need and my begging."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: al-qani' is the poor man who goes around asking, and al-mu'tarr is the visiting friend who visits to partake of the budn.

Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: al-qani' is the one who is greedy; al-mu'tarr is the one who comes for the budn, whether rich or poor.

Ibn Zayd: al-qani' is the needy one, and al-mu'tarr is the one who visits the people for their meat, and is not poor and does not have a sacrifice of his own; he comes to the people for the sake of their meat.

Al-Hasan read: ﴿wal-mu'tari﴾, which is like al-mu'tarr. It is said: 'araka and i'taraka when he comes to you seeking your favor.

﴿Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may be grateful﴾.

﴿It is not their meat that reaches Allah, nor their blood, but it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾. This is because the people of jahiliyyah, when they slaughtered the budn, would smear the walls of the Ka'bah with their blood. So Allah, glorified is He, revealed: ﴿It is not their meat that reaches Allah﴾, meaning does not reach Allah, ﴿nor their blood﴾.

﴿But it is piety from you that reaches Him﴾, meaning the intention, sincerity, and what is intended for the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He. Ya'qub read ﴿tanal﴾ and ﴿tanaluhu﴾ with the ta', and others with the ya'.

﴿Thus﴾, meaning in this way, ﴿He has subjected them﴾, meaning the budn, ﴿to you, that you may glorify Allah for having guided you﴾ to the markers of His religion and the rites of His Hajj. This means that you say, "Allahu akbar for what He has guided us to, and al-hamdu lillah for what He has tried us with and granted us."

And command (O Muhammad) ... Meaning: We also charged Ibrahim (peace be upon him) that he should proclaim (adhdhin) (i.e., inform and call out) among the people concerning the Hajj.

Ibrahim said, "O Lord, how would my voice reach (them)?" He said, "The proclamation is incumbent upon you, and the delivery is upon Me." So Ibrahim stood upon the Maqam, and it was said (he stood) on the mountain of Abu Qubays, and he called out: "O people! Your Lord has built a House, so make pilgrimage to it." Allah made that audible to those in the loins of men and the wombs of women, and to all between East and West, land and sea, those whom Allah, glorified is He, had decreed in His knowledge would perform the Hajj until the Day of Resurrection. They responded, "Here I am, O Allah, here I am."

Ibn 'Abbas said: By "the people" in this verse is meant the people of the qiblah (the Muslims). Al-Hasan claimed that the words of the Exalted, ﴿And proclaim among the people the Hajj﴾, are a new statement (kalam mustanaf), and that the one commanded to this proclamation is Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who was ordered to do so during the Farewell Pilgrimage.

﴿They will come to you on foot﴾: the plural of rajil (one on foot), like qa'im and qiyam, and sa'im and siyam.

﴿And upon every lean camel﴾: meaning, and riding. Dhamir is the emaciated camel. The plural form ﴿they will come﴾ (ya'tina) is used because of kull (every), meaning the female camels. ﴿From every deep ravine﴾: a distant path.

I heard Abu al-Hasan Muhammad ibn al-Qasim al-Faqih say: I heard Abu al-Qasim Bishr ibn Muhammad ibn Yasin al-Qadi say: "I saw in the tawaf an elderly man whom worship had exhausted, his color turned yellow, with a staff in his hand, circling the House while leaning on it. I approached him and began to ask him. He said to me, 'Where are you from?' I said, 'From Khurasan.' He said, 'In what region is Khurasan?' as if he did not know it. I said, 'A region of the eastern lands.' He said, 'How long do you take to cover this journey?' I said, 'Two or three months.' He said, 'Do you not perform Hajj every year, since you are neighbors of this House?' I said to him, 'And how far is it between you and this House?' He said, 'A five-year journey. I left my land when there was no white in my head or beard.' I said, 'By Allah, this is a manifest exertion, a beautiful obedience, and a true love.' He smiled in my face and recited:

Visit the one you love, even if the home is far away
and between you and him are veils and curtains.
Distance should not prevent you from visiting him,
for the lover is always a visitor to the one he desires.
[Al-'Uhud al-Muhammadiyya – al-Sha'rani: 437.]

﴿That they may witness﴾: that they may be present. ﴿Benefits for them﴾: meaning trade. This is from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, and it is the narration of Ibn Ruzayn from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: they are the markets.

Mujahid: trade, and what pleases Allah, glorified is He, of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, 'Ata' al-'Awfi, and Muhammad ibn 'Ali al-Baqir: pardon and forgiveness.

﴿And mention the name of Allah on known days﴾: meaning the days of Dhu al-Hijjah according to the view of most exegetes. The ﴿counted days﴾ are the days of tashriq (the days after 'Id al-Adha). They were called "counted" (ma'dudat) because they are few. It was said that the ten days are called "known" (ma'lumat) out of eagerness to know them by reckoning, because the time of Hajj is at their end.

Muqatil said: "The known days are the days of tashriq."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b: "The counted and the known are one and the same."

﴿Over what He has provided for them from the cattle of livestock﴾: meaning the offerings (hada') and sacrificial animals (dahaya) of camels, cows, and sheep.

﴿So eat from them﴾: an imperative of permission, not obligation. The exegetes said: He said this because the people of jahiliyyah used to slaughter their offerings and would not eat anything from the meat of their offerings.

﴿And feed the miserable one﴾: meaning the one afflicted (zamin), the poor one who has nothing. ﴿Then let them complete their (state of) unkemptness﴾ (thumma li-yaqdu): the readers differed on these lam's. Some pronounced them with a kasrah to distinguish thumma from waw and fa', and al-Farra' did so because thumma is a separated part of speech, while waw and fa' are like part of the same word. Others pronounced them with a sukun because they are all lam of command. ﴿Their unkemptness (tafath)﴾: "tafath" means:

All the rites of Hajj, according to Ibn 'Umar and Ibn 'Abbas.

Al-Qurazi and Mujahid said: it is the rites of Hajj, trimming the mustache, plucking the armpit hair, shaving the pubic hair, and cutting the nails.

'Ikrimah: tafath is hair and nails.

Al-Walibi, from Ibn 'Abbas: it is removing the state of ihram: shaving the head, cutting the nails, wearing clothes, and similar things. The original meaning of tafath in the language is filth. The Arabs say to a man whom they find disgusting, "How dirty you are (ma atfathaka)!" meaning, "How filthy you are! How repulsive you are!" Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt said:

Their armpits were clean; they had not been soiled by filth,
and they had removed from themselves lice and nits.
[Tafsir al-Qurtubi: 12/50.]

﴿And let them fulfill their vows﴾: Mujahid said: the vow of Hajj and of the offering, and whatever a person vows of something that is part of the Hajj.

﴿And let them circumambulate the Ancient House﴾: meaning the obligatory tawaf, which is the tawaf al-ifadah (the tawaf of return or visitation), performed after the 'Arafat stay, whether on the day of sacrifice or after it. The scholars differed on the meaning of "ancient" (atiq). Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn al-Zubayr, Mujahid, and Qatadah said: it was called ancient because Allah, glorified is He, freed it (a'taqahu) from tyrants who would reach to destroy it. No tyrant ever overpowered it, and no one was empowered over it except those who would venerate and respect it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Tubba' came intending to demolish the House. When he reached Qudayd, he was struck with paralysis. He called the rabbis, and they said: "This House has a Lord. No one who intends evil toward it is spared from being struck with harm by Him. If you want to be saved from what has befallen you, do not approach it with evil." He said: So he sent a gift to the House, a covering and leather hides, and it was the first thing to be covered. He slaughtered a thousand camels there, pardoned his people, honored them, and kept ties with them. Thus the place was called al-Matabikh (the kitchens) for the cooking of the people; his horses were excellent, so it was named Jiyad for the horses of Tubba'; and Qu'ayqi'an was named for the clatter of weapons when he came from Madinah.

Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah said: It was named so because it was never owned (lam yumlak qatt). This is also the narration of 'Ubayd from Mujahid, who said: "The House was named 'ancient' only because no one has any possession in it."

Ibn Zayd said: because it is ancient, and it is the first house placed for the people. It is said: a sword that is atiq (old) or a dinar that is atiq, meaning old. It was also said: because it is noble before Allah, glorified is He. The Arabs say: a horse that is atiq (noble).

﴿That (is so). And whoever honors the sacred rites of Allah﴾, by avoiding His disobedience, ﴿it is better for him in the sight of his Lord﴾.

Ibn Zayd said: The sacred things (hurumat) are al-Mash'ar al-Haram, the Sacred House, the Sacred Mosque, and the Sacred City. It was also said: they are the rites (manasik).

﴿And lawful to you are the cattle (an'am)﴾ to eat when you have slaughtered them, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ in the Qur'an, which is His saying: ﴿Prohibited to you are carrion and blood﴾ [5:3] to the end of the verse, and His saying: ﴿And do not eat of that over which the name of Allah has not been mentioned﴾ [6:121]. It was also said: ﴿And lawful to you are the cattle﴾ during your state of ihram, ﴿except what is recited to you﴾ concerning game, for it is forbidden during the state of ihram.

﴿So avoid the filth of idols﴾: meaning worshipping them, because all idols are filth.

﴿And avoid the speech of falsehood﴾: meaning lying and slander.

Ayman ibn Hurrayn said: The Prophet (ﷺ) gave a sermon and said: "O people! The false testimony has been made equal to associating partners with Allah," then he recited this verse. [5] [Musnad Ahmad: 4/178.]

Some of them said: it is the statement of the polytheists in their talbiyah: "Here I am, You have no partner, except a partner who is Yours; You own him and what he owns."

﴿Ḥunafa'﴾: upright, sincere, devoted to Allah. It was also said: pilgrims. ﴿Not associating anything with Him﴾. ﴿And whoever associates with Allah, it is as if he had fallen from the sky﴾, meaning he dropped to the earth, ﴿and the birds snatch him away﴾. The words khatf and ikhtitaf mean taking something swiftly. The people of Madinah read ﴿fatakhattafuhu﴾ with a fatha on the kha' and shaddah on the ta', meaning tatakhattafuhu, and they assimilated the letters. The reading of the general readers is confirmed by His saying: ﴿except one who snatches a snatch﴾ [37:10].

﴿Or the wind carries him off to a distant place﴾: meaning far away.

The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: The condition of the polytheist is compared to that of one who falls, in that he possesses no benefit for himself and no removal of harm on the Day of Resurrection.

Al-Hasan said: The deeds of the disbelievers are compared to this state, in that they are swept away and nullified, so they are unable to achieve anything from them.

﴿That (is so)﴾, meaning what I have mentioned of avoiding filth and falsehood and glorifying the rites of Allah, ﴿is from the piety of hearts﴾. This is the meaning and arrangement of the verse. The rites of Allah (sha'a'ir Allah) are the offerings (hady) and the camels (budn). The root is from ish'ar (marking), which is announcing them so that they may be recognized as offerings, and they are named after it. Glorifying them means deeming them great, finding them beautiful, and choosing them to be fat.

﴿For you in them﴾, meaning in the offerings, ﴿are benefits﴾. It was said: that their owner names them a budnah or hady, marks them, and garlands them, and you may benefit from their milk, wool, and fur, and ride upon their backs. ﴿Until a specified term﴾: which is that once he names it an offering and makes it obligatory, then when he does so, he has no benefit from them. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ata', al-Dahhak, and Qatadah, and the narration of Muqsim from Ibn 'Abbas. It was also said: the meaning is that in these offerings there are benefits for you after they are brought forth and named as offerings, by riding them when you need to, and drinking their milk if you are compelled to, ﴿until a specified term﴾, meaning until they are slaughtered. This is the view of 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah.

Some of them said: By the rites (sha'a'ir) he meant the manasik and the sacred sites of Makkah. The meaning of the verse: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through trade and markets, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is leaving Makkah. This is the narration of Abu Dharr from Ibn 'Abbas.

Some of them said: ﴿For you in them are benefits﴾ through reward and recompense in performing the rites and establishing the rites of Hajj, ﴿until a specified term﴾, which is the end of the days of Hajj.

﴿Then their place of sacrifice is at the Ancient House﴾: meaning their place of slaughter is near the Ancient House, that is, the whole land of the Haram. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿So let them not approach the Sacred Mosque after this year﴾ [9:28], meaning the entire Haram. The phrase "cattle of livestock" is specified because among beasts there are some that are not livestock, such as horses, mules, and donkeys. Beasts (bahaʾim) is so named because they cannot speak.

﴿Your God is one God, so submit to Him. And give good tidings to the humble (mukhbitin)﴾. Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah said: the humble, the modest. Mujahid: those at peace with Allah, glorified is He. Al-Akhfash: the humbled. Ibn Jarir: the submissive. 'Amr ibn Aws: those who do not wrong, and if they are wronged, they do not seek retribution.

﴿Those whose hearts tremble when Allah is mentioned, and those who are patient over what befalls them, and those who establish prayer, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾. ﴿And the camels (budn)﴾, meaning the large, massive-bodied camels. 'Ata' and al-Suddi said: al-budn: the camels and the cows.

﴿We have made them for you among the rites of Allah﴾, meaning the markers of His religion when they are marked. ﴿For you in them is good﴾: benefit in this world, and reward in the Hereafter. ﴿So mention the name of Allah over them﴾ at the time of their slaughter. Ibn 'Abbas said: it is to say, "Allahu akbar, la ilaha illa Allah, wa Allahu akbar, Allahumma minka wa laka."

﴿Standing in rows (sawaff)﴾: meaning standing on three legs, with their feet arranged and one of their forelegs bound, and the left foreleg tied, so the animal is slaughtered in that position.

Yala ibn 'Ata' narrated from Yahya ibn Salim, who said: "I saw Ibn 'Umar slaughtering his camel, and he said, 'Standing in rows, as Allah, glorified is He, said.' He slaughtered it while it was standing and tied, one of its forelegs bound."

Mujahid said: "Sawaff" means when its left hind leg is tied, and it stands on three legs, and it is slaughtered in that manner.

Ibn Mas'ud read: ﴿sawafin﴾, which means those tied by one foreleg, and it stands on three legs and is slaughtered; it is like sawaff. Ubayy read: ﴿sawafi﴾, and likewise Mujahid and Zayd ibn Aslam with the ya', meaning pure and sincere for Allah, glorified is He, with no partner in them, as the polytheists used to do.

﴿So when they have fallen on their sides (wajabat junubuha)﴾, meaning when they fall after slaughter and their sides come to rest on the ground.

﴿Thus We have subjected them to you, that you may be grateful﴾.

This means that you say, "Allahu akbar for what He has guided us to, and al-hamdu lillah for what He has tried us with and granted us."

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 22, verse 38–47:

Inna Allah yudafi'u (Makki and Basri read yadfa'u; the others read yudafi'u), and its meaning is: indeed Allah repels the calamity of the polytheists

ʿani alladhina amanu. Inna Allah la yuhibbu kulla khawwanin (treacherous) fi amanat Allah, kafurin li-ni'matihi (ungrateful for His blessing).

Udhina: the people of Madina, Basra and ʿAsim read udhina with a damma on the alif; the rest read it with a fatha, meaning Allah has permitted (those who are fought) — lil-ladhina yuqatalun. The people of Madina and Syria read it with a fatha on the ta', meaning the believers who are confronted by the polytheists; the rest read it with a kasra on the ta', meaning that those to whom permission for jihad was given fight the polytheists. Bi-annahum zululu wa inna Allah ʿala nasrihim la-qadir (because they were wronged, and indeed Allah is capable of giving them victory).

The exegetes said: The polytheists of Makka used to harm the Companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so they kept coming to him from among those who had been beaten and wounded, complaining of them to the Messenger of Allah, and he would say to them: "Be patient, for I have not been commanded to fight until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ emigrates from Makka." Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed this verse, and it is the first verse in which Allah permitted fighting.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: When the Prophet ﷺ was driven out of Makka, Abu Bakr said: "They have expelled their Prophet! Inna lillahi wa inna ilayhi raji'un (indeed we belong to Allah and to Him we return); we shall surely perish." Then Allah, glorified is He, revealed udhina lil-ladhina yuqatalun, the verse. Abu Bakr said: "I knew then that there would be fighting."

Mujahid said: This verse was revealed concerning specific people who went out as emigrants from Makka to Madina, and they were prevented from emigrating, so Allah, exalted is He, permitted them to fight the disbelievers who were preventing them from emigrating.

Alladhina ukhrijus min diyarihim bi-ghayri haqq (those who were expelled from their homes without right) is a substitute (badal) for the first alladhina. Then He said illa an yaqulu rabbuna Allah (except that they say: Our Lord is Allah), meaning they were not expelled from their homes except for their saying "Our Lord is Allah alone." So "an" is in the genitive position, as a response to the ba' in bi-ghayri haqq. It is also permissible that it be in the accusative position as an exception (istithna').

Wa lawla daf'u Allahi al-nas ba'dahum bi-ba'd (and were it not for Allah's repelling people, some by means of others) — through jihad, the establishment of the prescribed punishments, and the restraint of oppression — la-huddimat (there would surely have been demolished): the Hijazis read it with the dal lightened, and the rest with it doubled, on the kasra, meaning destroyed, sawami'u (monasteries). Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: this means the monasteries of the monks. Qatada: the monasteries of the Sabians.

Wa biya'un (churches) of the Christians. Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: al-biya' are the synagogues of the Jews, and Ibn Zayd said the same.

Wa salawat: Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatada and al-Dahhak said: this means the synagogues of the Jews, which they call "salwata." Abu al-ʿAliya said: they are the places of worship (masajid) of the Sabians.

Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid: they are places of worship for the People of the Book and for the people of Islam on the road. According to these sayings, the salawat (prayers) are the prayers of the people of Islam, which are interrupted when the enemy enters upon them: worship ceases and the mosques are demolished, as Bukhtnassar did.

Wa masajidu yudhkaru fiha ism Allahi kathiran (and mosques in which the name of Allah is much mentioned): this means the mosques of the Muslims. It was also said that its interpretation is: "would surely have been demolished monasteries and churches" in the days of the sharia of Jesus, "and prayer-places" in the days of the sharia of Moses, "and mosques" in the days of the sharia of Muhammad, may Allah's blessings be upon them all.

Al-Hasan said: He repels the demolition of the places of prayer of the People of Dhimma by means of the believers. If it is asked: why did He mention the places of prayer of the disbelievers before the mosques of the Muslims? We say: because they are older. It was also said: because they are closer to demolition, and the mosques are closer to remembrance, just as He placed the foremost (al-sabiq) later in His saying: fa-minhum zalimun li-nafsihi (among them is one who wrongs himself), because he is closer to the good deeds (al-khayrat) [in the second copy: al-hasanat].

Wa la-yansuranna Allahu man yansuruhu (and Allah will surely help whoever helps Him): that is, whoever helps His religion and His Prophet.

Inna Allaha la-qawiyyun ʿazizun (indeed Allah is strong and mighty). Alladhina in makkannahum fi al-ardi aqamu al-salata wa atawu al-zakata wa amaru bi-al-maʿruf wa nahaw ʿan al-munkar (those who, if We establish them in the land, establish prayer, give zakat, enjoin good and forbid evil). Qatada said: they are the Companions of Muhammad. ʿIkrima: the people of the five daily prayers. Al-Hasan and Abu al-ʿAliya: this community.

Wa lillahi ʿaqibatu al-umur (and to Allah belongs the final outcome of affairs): the last of the affairs of creation and their return to Him.

Wa in yukadhdhibuka ya Muhammad fa-qad kadhdhabat qablahum qawmu Nuhin wa ʿAdun wa Thamudu wa qawmu Ibrahima wa qawmu Lutin wa ashabu Madyana wa kudhdhiba Musa fa-amlaytu lil-kafirina (I gave them respite) thumma akhadhtuhum (I seized them; their outcome) fa-kayfa kana nakir (how was My rejection): My denial, by way of punishment and destruction. He consoles His Prophet ﷺ and warns those who oppose him.

Fa-ka'ayyin (how many) wa kam min qaryatin ahlaknaha wa hiya zalimatun (while it was wrongdoing): meaning and its people were wrongdoers, and the wrongdoing is attributed to the town because of the nearness of its neighborhood.

Fa-hiya khawiyatun ʿala ʿurushiha (fallen upon its roofs), wa bi'rin mu'attalatin (abandoned, left empty of its people), wa qasrin mashid. Qatada, al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: lofty and tall. From it is the saying of ʿAdi [in the second copy: ʿAli ibn Zayd]:

Shadahu marmaran wa jallalahu kalsan... fa-lil-tayri fi dhurahu wukur
(He built it of marble and plastered it with gypsum, so the birds have nests on its heights.) [Lisan al-ʿArab: 3/244.]

That is, he raised it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Mujahid, ʿAta' and ʿIkrima said: plastered with lime (mujassas), from al-shid, which is lime (al-jass). The rajaz poet says:

Like a drop of water between the mortar and the lime.

Imru' al-Qays said:

And Tayma', in which no palm-trunk was left, nor a fortress except built up with stones and lime. [Lisan al-ʿArab: 12/8.]

That is, built with lime and stones.

Abu Rawq related from al-Dahhak that this well was in Hadramawt, in a town called Hasura. Four thousand men who had believed in Salih and been saved from the punishment came to Hadramawt with Salih, and when they arrived Salih died; therefore it was named Hadramawt, because when Salih was present there he died. They built Hasura and settled beside this well, and they appointed over themselves a man called Balhanas ibn Jallas ibn Suwayd, and made his vizier Sanharib ibn Sawada. They remained for a long time and multiplied until they grew and increased. Then they worshipped idols and disbelieved, so Allah sent to them a prophet called Hanzala ibn Safwan, who was a porter among them, and they killed him in the market. Then Allah destroyed them, their well was abandoned, and their palaces were laid waste.

Afa lam yasiru fi al-ardi (have they not traveled through the land), meaning the disbelievers of Makka, so that they might look at the places of destruction of the deniers from the past nations.

Fa-takunu lahum qulubun yaʿqiluna biha (so that they have hearts by which they understand), meaning they know by them, aw adhanun yasmaʿuna biha (or ears by which they hear), so that they reflect and take warning.

Fa-inna ha la ta'ma al-absaru wa lakin ta'ma al-qulubu allati fi al-sudur (indeed it is not the eyes that go blind, but the hearts within the breasts that go blind). This is emphasis, like His saying: wa la ta'irin yatiru bi-janahayhi (nor any bird that flies with its two wings), and His saying: yaqulina bi-afwahihim (they say with their mouths).

Ibn ʿAbbas and Muqatil said: When He revealed wa man kana fi hadhihi a'ma fa-huwa fi al-akhirati a'ma (whoever is blind in this world will be blind in the Hereafter), Ibn Umm Maktum came weeping to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I am blind in this world; shall I be blind in the Hereafter?"

Then Allah, glorified and exalted is He, revealed this verse.

Wa yasta'jiluna-ka bi-al-adhab (and they seek to hasten the punishment from you): it was revealed concerning al-Nadr ibn al-Harith.

Wa lan yukhlifa Allahu wa'dahu (and Allah will never fail His promise): He fulfilled that on the day of Badr.

Wa inna yawman ʿinda rabbika ka-alfi sanatin mimma taʿuddun (indeed a day with your Lord is like a thousand years of what you count): read with the ya' by Makki and Kufis except ʿAsim; the rest read it with the ta'.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: it refers to the days in which Allah, glorified is He, created the heavens and the earth. Mujahid and ʿIkrima: it refers to the days of the Hereafter.

Ibn Zayd, regarding His saying wa inna yawman ʿinda rabbika ka-alfi sanatin mimma taʿuddun, said: these are the days of the Hereafter.

And regarding His saying: ta'ruju al-malaikatu wa al-ruhu ilayhi fi yawmin kana miqdaruhu khamsina alfa sanah (the angels and the Spirit ascend to Him in a day whose measure is fifty thousand years), he said: that is the Day of Resurrection.

Ahl al-maʿani (the scholars of meanings) said: the meaning of the verse is: indeed a day with your Lord, from among the days of the punishment they sought to hasten, is in its heaviness, length and severity like a thousand years of what you count. So how would you hasten it? This is like saying: the days of sorrow are long, and the days of joy are short.

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 22, verses 48–60:

﴿How many a town have I given respite while it was wrongdoing, then I seized it, and to Me is the final return. Say: O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you. As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, there is forgiveness for them and generous provision. But those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ "Sa'aw fi ayatina" means they worked to nullify Our signs. "Mu'ajizin" means opposing and contending. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Akhfash said: "mut'annifin" (those who seek to make them appear weak, i.e., those who obstruct). Qatadah said: they thought they could escape Allah, so He would not have power over them, and they would never escape Him.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "mu'ajjizin" with a shaddah, meaning those who discourage people from faith. The same form occurs in Surah Saba.

﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire. We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he desired (tamanna), Satan threw into his desire.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and other exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw his people turning away from him, and was distressed by their rejection of what had come to him from Allah the Exalted, he wished within himself that something would come to him from Allah that would bring him closer to his people, out of his eagerness for their faith. One day he sat in one of the assemblies of Quraysh, which had many people. He wished that nothing would come to him from Allah the Exalted that would drive them away from him, and he desired that. Then Allah the Exalted sent down Surah al-Najm: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 1]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 19–20]. Satan cast upon his tongue, as he was speaking what he was saying to himself and wishing for: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued his recitation, reciting the whole surah, and prostrated at its end. So the Muslims prostrated with his prostration, and all those in the mosque of the polytheists prostrated too. Not a believer nor a disbeliever remained in the mosque without prostrating, except al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Uhayhah Sa'id ibn al-'As. They each took a handful of the gravel of al-Batha' and raised it to their foreheads and prostrated upon it, because they were two elderly men who could not prostrate. Quraysh dispersed, pleased with what they had heard, and said: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods with the best mention." They also said: "We know that Allah gives life and causes death, creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him. So if Muhammad makes a share for them, we are with him."

When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was visited by Jibril (peace be upon him), who said: "O Muhammad, what have you done?! You have recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah, and you said what He did not say to you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was then greatly grieved and feared Allah with great fear. So Allah the Exalted sent down this verse.

Those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were in the land of Abyssinia heard of this, and it reached them that Quraysh had prostrated. It was said: "Quraysh and the people of Makkah have embraced Islam." So most of them returned to their tribes, saying: "They are more beloved to us." They found the people had reverted to disbelief after Allah had abrogated what Satan had cast. Then Allah the Exalted sent down Surah al-Najm: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 1]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 19–20]. Satan cast upon his tongue, as he was speaking what he was saying to himself and wishing for: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued his recitation, reciting the whole surah, and prostrated at its end. So the Muslims prostrated with his prostration, and all those in the mosque of the polytheists prostrated too. Not a believer nor a disbeliever remained in the mosque without prostrating, except al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Uhayhah Sa'id ibn al-'As. They each took a handful of the gravel of al-Batha' and raised it to their foreheads and prostrated upon it, because they were two elderly men who could not prostrate. Quraysh dispersed, pleased with what they had heard, and said: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods with the best mention." They also said: "We know that Allah gives life and causes death, creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him. So if Muhammad makes a share for them, we are with him."

When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was visited by Jibril (peace be upon him), who said: "O Muhammad, what have you done?! You have recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah, and you said what He did not say to you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was then greatly grieved and feared Allah with great fear. So Allah the Exalted sent down this verse.

Those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were in the land of Abyssinia heard of this, and it reached them that Quraysh had prostrated. It was said: "Quraysh and the people of Makkah have embraced Islam." So most of them returned to their tribes, saying: "They are more beloved to us." They found the people had reverted to disbelief after Allah had abrogated what Satan had cast. When this verse was revealed, Quraysh said: "Muhammad regrets what he said about the status of our gods with Allah, so he changed it and brought something else." The two phrases that Satan had cast upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had spread into the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil beyond what they had been upon, and in hostility toward those who embraced Islam. [Ibn al-'Arabi, in his tafsir Ahkam al-Qur'an, denied the story of the cranes, because it involves Satan's interference in the teachings of Islam and his domination over the Prophet of mercy, who "does not speak from desire."]

﴿And We did not send before you any messenger﴾, namely one to whom Jibril brings revelation face to face and orally, ﴿nor any prophet﴾, namely one whose prophethood is by inspiration or dream, ﴿except that when he desired﴾, meaning he loved something and longed for it, and spoke to himself about what he was not commanded.

﴿Satan threw into his desire﴾, meaning into his aim, and found a way to it. Most exegetes said: by His saying "tamanna" (تَمَنَّى), it means recited and read the Book of Allah the Exalted. ﴿Satan threw into his desire﴾ means into his recitation and reading. A parallel is His saying: ﴿They know not the Book except as wishful recitations (amani)﴾ [Surah al-Baqarah: 78], meaning readings that are read to them.

A poet said about 'Uthman, may Allah be pleased with him, when he was killed:

"He recited the Book of Allah at the first night,
and its last recitation met the doom of fate."
[Kitab al-'Ayn: 8/390]

I heard Abu al-Qasim al-Habib say: I heard Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Mahdi [in the second copy: ibn al-Saddi] al-Tabari say:
"This wishing (tamanni) is not part of the Qur'an or revelation at all. Rather, when the Prophet (ﷺ) had an empty hand of wealth and saw the bad condition of his Companions, he wished for the world in his heart, a whispering from Satan."

Al-Hasan said: by "al-gharaniq al-'ula" he meant the angels, meaning that intercession is hoped for from them and not from the idols. But this view is neither strong nor accepted, because of His saying: ﴿Then Allah abrogates what Satan throws, then Allah makes His verses firm﴾, meaning He nullifies and removes it, then Allah firmly establishes His verses, and Allah is All-Knowing, All-Wise.

If it is asked: what is the reason for permitting error in recitation upon the Prophet (ﷺ)? There are two answers:

The first: it was by way of forgetfulness and slip of the tongue, and Allah will soon alert him and protect him.

The second: Satan said that during the Prophet's recitation, giving the impression that it was from the Qur'an and that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was the one reciting it. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿That He may make what Satan throws a trial for those in whose hearts is a disease﴾, so that they would doubt it.

﴿And the hardened hearts﴾, so they do not soften to the command of Allah. ﴿Indeed, the wrongdoers, the disbelievers, are in far-reaching opposition.﴾ ﴿And that those given knowledge, among the believers, may know that it is the truth from your Lord, so that they believe in it and their hearts humble before Him.﴾ That is, that what Allah the Exalted made firm of the verses of the Qur'an is the truth from your Lord. ﴿Indeed, Allah guides those who believe to a straight path.﴾ ﴿And those who disbelieve will not cease to be in doubt about it﴾, meaning about what Satan cast upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).

Ibn Juraij said: "from the Qur'an." Others said: "from the religion, which is the straight path."

﴿Until the Hour comes upon them suddenly, or there comes upon them the punishment of a barren day.﴾ 'Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: the punishment of a day without a night, which is the Day of Resurrection.

Others said: it is the day of Badr, and this is the correct view, because the Hour is the Resurrection, and there is no sense in saying "until the Resurrection comes upon them." It was called "barren" (aqim) because they did not see the night on it, rather they were killed before evening, said Ibn Juraij. Others said: because there was no mercy or compassion in it. It was also said: because there was no equal to it in the greatness of its matter, given the fighting of the angels in it.

﴿The dominion that day﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, ﴿belongs to Allah alone﴾, without any rival or claimant. Dominion is the breadth of power for the one who holds the management of affairs. Allah the Exalted is the One who truly possesses all affairs, and every other dominion is granted by His command and permission.

﴿He will judge between them﴾. Then He explained His judgment, saying, Mighty is He: ﴿So those who believed and did righteous deeds will be in Gardens of Bliss, and those who disbelieved and denied Our signs, for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾ ﴿And those who emigrated in the cause of Allah, meaning who left their homelands and tribes in obedience to Allah the Exalted and seeking His pleasure, then were killed or died while in that state, Allah will surely provide for them a goodly provision in Paradise. And indeed, Allah is the best of providers.﴾ It was also said: this refers to His saying: ﴿Rather, they are alive with their Lord, being provided for﴾ [Surah Al 'Imran: 169].

Ibn Wahb narrated from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj ibn Salaman ibn 'Amir, who said: Fudalah ibn Dus was an emir over the quarters. He went out with the funerals of two men: one was killed and the other died naturally. He saw people inclining toward the funeral of the one who was killed, going to his grave, and he said: "I see you, O people, inclining toward the one who was killed and preferring him over his brother who died! By Him in whose hand is my soul, I do not care in which grave of them I am raised. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 22, verses 48–60:

﴿How many a town have I given respite while it was wrongdoing, then I seized it, and to Me is the final return. Say: O mankind, I am only a clear warner to you. As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, there is forgiveness for them and generous provision. But those who strive against Our signs, seeking to frustrate them, they are the companions of the Blazing Fire.﴾ "Sa'aw fi ayatina" means they worked to nullify Our signs. "Mu'ajizin" means opposing and contending. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Akhfash said: "mut'annifin" (those who seek to make them appear weak, i.e., those who obstruct). Qatadah said: they thought they could escape Allah, so He would not have power over them, and they would never escape Him.

Ibn Kathir and Abu 'Amr recited "mu'ajjizin" with a shaddah, meaning those who discourage people from faith. The same form occurs in Surah Saba.

﴿Those are the companions of the Hellfire. We did not send before you any messenger or prophet except that when he desired (tamanna), Satan threw into his desire.﴾

Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, and other exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) saw his people turning away from him, and was distressed by their rejection of what had come to him from Allah the Exalted, he wished within himself that something would come to him from Allah that would bring him closer to his people, out of his eagerness for their faith. One day he sat in one of the assemblies of Quraysh, which had many people. He wished that nothing would come to him from Allah the Exalted that would drive them away from him, and he desired that. Then Allah the Exalted sent down Surah al-Najm: ﴿By the star when it sets﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 1]. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited it until he reached: ﴿Have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other one?﴾ [Surah al-Najm: 19–20]. Satan cast upon his tongue, as he was speaking what he was saying to himself and wishing for: "Those are the exalted cranes, and their intercession is to be hoped for."

When Quraysh heard that, they rejoiced. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) continued his recitation, reciting the whole surah, and prostrated at its end. So the Muslims prostrated with his prostration, and all those in the mosque of the polytheists prostrated too. Not a believer nor a disbeliever remained in the mosque without prostrating, except al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and Abu Uhayhah Sa'id ibn al-'As. They each took a handful of the gravel of al-Batha' and raised it to their foreheads and prostrated upon it, because they were two elderly men who could not prostrate. Quraysh dispersed, pleased with what they had heard, and said: "Muhammad has mentioned our gods with the best mention." They also said: "We know that Allah gives life and causes death, creates and provides, but these gods of ours intercede for us with Him. So if Muhammad makes a share for them, we are with him."

When evening came, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was visited by Jibril (peace be upon him), who said: "O Muhammad, what have you done?! You have recited to the people what I did not bring you from Allah, and you said what He did not say to you." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was then greatly grieved and feared Allah with great fear. So Allah the Exalted sent down this verse.

Those among the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) who were in the land of Abyssinia heard of this, and it reached them that Quraysh had prostrated. It was said: "Quraysh and the people of Makkah have embraced Islam." So most of them returned to their tribes, saying: "They are more beloved to us." They found the people had reverted to disbelief after Allah had abrogated what Satan had cast. When this verse was revealed, Quraysh said: "Muhammad regrets what he said about the status of our gods with Allah, so he changed it and brought something else." The two phrases that Satan had cast upon the tongue of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had spread into the mouth of every polytheist, so they increased in evil beyond what they had been upon, and in hostility toward those who embraced Islam. [Ibn al-'Arabi, in his tafsir Ahkam al-Qur'an, denied the story of the cranes, because it involves Satan's interference in the teachings of Islam and his domination over the Prophet of mercy, who "does not speak from desire."]

Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 22, verse 73–78:

يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ

Ma'na ḍaraba (ضرب): ja'ala (made, appointed), as in their saying: ḍaraba al-sulṭān al-baʿth ʿalā al-nās (the ruler imposed the levy on the people), and ḍaraba al-jizya ʿalā ahl al-dhimma (he imposed the poll-tax on the protected people), meaning he made that incumbent upon them. From it is His saying: ﴿وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 61.]] (﴿And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them﴾). The mathal (مثل, parable, similitude) is a fixed state that is likened to another in a mention that has become like a proper name; its origin is resemblance (al-shabah). The meaning of the verse: the polytheists made the idols their partners, so they worshipped them alongside Him.

فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ

Its state, its description, which I have clarified and likened to it.

ثم بيّن ذلك فقال عزّ من قائل

Then He explained that, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks:

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ

The common reading is with the ta' (تدعون, "you call upon"). Zayd related from Ya'qub the reading yadʿūna (يدعون, with the ya').

لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُباباً

In its smallness and insignificance, because it cannot do that.

وَلَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا لَهُ

To create it. Dhubāb (الذباب) is singular; its paucal plural is adhinna (أذبنة) and its plural of multitude is dhubbān (ذبّان), like ghurāb (غراب), aghriba (أغربة), and ghirbān (غربان).

وَإِنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ

That is, the idols; He reported about them with a verb of rational beings, and this matter has already passed. He says:

الذُّبابُ شَيْئاً مما عليهم لا يقدرون أن يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ وَالْمَطْلُوبُ.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the idol. That is because the disbelievers used to smear their idols with honey every year, then they would shut the doors of the houses upon them, so the flies would enter through the openings and eat that honey and clean it off. When they saw that, they said: "Our gods have eaten the honey."

al-Ḍaḥḥāk: it means the worshipper and the worshipped.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan: they used to adorn the idols with rubies, pearls, and kinds of jewels, and perfume them with various scents; so sometimes one of these would fall off, or a bird or a fly would take it, and the gods could not recover it. So the seeker, on this interpretation, is the idol and the sought is the fly or the bird.

مَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ

That is, they did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, nor did they describe Him with the description due to Him, since they associated with Him that which cannot even withstand a fly nor avenge itself upon it.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ

ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي

Yakhtār (chooses) from among the angels messengers, such as Jibril and Mika'il and others, and from among mankind also messengers, such as Ibrahim, Musa, ʿĪsā, Muhammad, and other prophets, may Allah's blessings be upon them. It is said: this verse was revealed when the polytheists said: ﴿أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا﴾ [[Sūrat al-Qamar: 25.]] (﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾). So He informed that the choosing is up to Him; He chooses whom He wills from among His creation.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ

Hearing their statement,

بَصِيرٌ

Seeing whom He chooses for His message.

يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ

That is, what was before the hands of His angels and messengers before He created them.

وَما خَلْفَهُمْ

And He knows what will be after their passing away.

وقال الحسن: ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ ما عملوه، وَما خَلْفَهُمْ ما هم عاملون ممّا لم يعملوه بعد.

al-Ḥasan said: ma bayna aydīhim is what they have done, and ma khalfahum is what they will do of what they have not yet done.

يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/317.]] .

Aḫbaranā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: Aḫbaranā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: and in what I read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, and Ḥaddathanī Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Mālik from Nāfiʿ that a man from the people of Egypt informed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) recited Sūrat al-Ḥajj and prostrated in it twice, then said: "Indeed this sūra has been favoured with two prostrations."

And with its isnād from Mālik from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, that he said: "I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar prostrate twice in al-Ḥajj."

And Aḫbaranā Abū Bakr al-Jawzaqī, who said: Aḫbaranā Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Daʿūlī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Abī Khaythama, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Salama al-Khuzāʿī Manṣūr ibn Salama, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ḥammād ibn Salama from ʿAlī ibn Zayd from Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān that Abū Mūsā recited Sūrat al-Ḥajj on the pulpit of Basra, then descended and prostrated in it twice.

And Ḥaddathanā Abū Muḥammad al-Mukhallidī, who said: Aḫbaranā ʿAbd Allāh ibn Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Muslim ibn Dāra, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Mūsā ibn Aʿyan, who said: I read to my father from ʿAmr ibn al-Ḥārith from Ibn Lahīʿa that Sharīḥ ibn ʿĀhā narrated to him from ʿUqba ibn ʿĀmir, who said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Sūrat al-Ḥajj have two prostrations?" He said: "Yes; if you do not prostrate them, then do not recite them."

وَجاهِدُوا فِي اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهادِهِ

That is, strive in the way of Allah against the enemies of Allah with the striving due to Him, which is exhausting one's capacity in it; so said Ibn ʿAbbas. And from him also: "Do not fear the blame of any blamer in Allah; that is the due striving."

Al-Ḍaḥḥāk and Muqātil said: it means act for Allah with the truth of His action, and worship Him with the truth of His worship.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mubārak: it is striving against the self and desire, and that is the due striving, which is the greater jihad, as is related in the report that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said when he returned from one of his expeditions: "We have returned from the lesser jihad to the greater jihad."[6] [[Fayḍ al-Qadīr, al-Manāwī: 3/141.]]

هُوَ اجْتَباكُمْ

He chose you for His religion.

وَما جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ

Ḥaraj means constriction. Commentary of al-Tha'alibi (al-Jawahir al-Hisan) on surah 22, verse 73–78:

يا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ

Ma'na ḍaraba (ضرب): ja'ala (made, appointed), as in their saying: ḍaraba al-sulṭān al-baʿth ʿalā al-nās (the ruler imposed the levy on the people), and ḍaraba al-jizya ʿalā ahl al-dhimma (he imposed the poll-tax on the protected people), meaning he made that incumbent upon them. From it is His saying: ﴿وَضُرِبَتْ عَلَيْهِمُ الذِّلَّةُ وَالْمَسْكَنَةُ﴾ [[Sūrat al-Baqara: 61.]] (﴿And humiliation and wretchedness were stamped upon them﴾). The mathal (مثل, parable, similitude) is a fixed state that is likened to another in a mention that has become like a proper name; its origin is resemblance (al-shabah). The meaning of the verse: the polytheists made the idols their partners, so they worshipped them alongside Him.

فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ

Its state, its description, which I have clarified and likened to it.

ثم بيّن ذلك فقال عزّ من قائل

Then He explained that, saying, Mighty is He Who speaks:

إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ

The common reading is with the ta' (تدعون, "you call upon"). Zayd related from Ya'qub the reading yadʿūna (يدعون, with the ya').

لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُباباً

In its smallness and insignificance, because it cannot do that.

وَلَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا لَهُ

To create it. Dhubāb (الذباب) is singular; its paucal plural is adhinna (أذبنة) and its plural of multitude is dhubbān (ذبّان), like ghurāb (غراب), aghriba (أغربة), and ghirbān (غربان).

وَإِنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ

That is, the idols; He reported about them with a verb of rational beings, and this matter has already passed. He says:

الذُّبابُ شَيْئاً مما عليهم لا يقدرون أن يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ وَالْمَطْلُوبُ.

Ibn ʿAbbas said: the seeker is the fly and the sought is the idol. That is because the disbelievers used to smear their idols with honey every year, then they would shut the doors of the houses upon them, so the flies would enter through the openings and eat that honey and clean it off. When they saw that, they said: "Our gods have eaten the honey."

al-Ḍaḥḥāk: it means the worshipper and the worshipped.

Ibn Zayd and Ibn Kaysan: they used to adorn the idols with rubies, pearls, and kinds of jewels, and perfume them with various scents; so sometimes one of these would fall off, or a bird or a fly would take it, and the gods could not recover it. So the seeker, on this interpretation, is the idol and the sought is the fly or the bird.

مَا قَدَرُوا اللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدْرِهِ

That is, they did not magnify Allah with the magnification due to Him, nor did they know Him with the knowledge due to Him, nor did they describe Him with the description due to Him, since they associated with Him that which cannot even withstand a fly nor avenge itself upon it.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ

ٱللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي

Yakhtār (chooses) from among the angels messengers, such as Jibril and Mika'il and others, and from among mankind also messengers, such as Ibrahim, Musa, ʿĪsā, Muhammad, and other prophets, may Allah's blessings be upon them. It is said: this verse was revealed when the polytheists said: ﴿أَأُلْقِيَ الذِّكْرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ بَيْنِنا﴾ [[Sūrat al-Qamar: 25.]] (﴿Has the Reminder been sent down to him from among us?﴾). So He informed that the choosing is up to Him; He chooses whom He wills from among His creation.

إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ

Hearing their statement,

بَصِيرٌ

Seeing whom He chooses for His message.

يَعْلَمُ ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ

That is, what was before the hands of His angels and messengers before He created them.

وَما خَلْفَهُمْ

And He knows what will be after their passing away.

وقال الحسن: ما بَيْنَ أَيْدِيهِمْ ما عملوه، وَما خَلْفَهُمْ ما هم عاملون ممّا لم يعملوه بعد.

al-Ḥasan said: ma bayna aydīhim is what they have done, and ma khalfahum is what they will do of what they have not yet done.

يا أَيُّهَا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا ارْكَعُوا وَاسْجُدُوا وَاعْبُدُوا رَبَّكُمْ وَافْعَلُوا الْخَيْرَ لَعَلَّكُمْ تُفْلِحُونَ [[al-Sunan al-Kubrā: 2/317.]] .

Aḫbaranā Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Yūsuf, who said: Aḫbaranā Makkī ibn ʿAbdān, who said: Ḥaddathanā Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā, who said: and in what I read to ʿAbd Allāh ibn Nāfiʿ, and Ḥaddathanī Muṭarrif ibn ʿAbd Allāh from Mālik from Nāfiʿ that a man from the people of Egypt informed ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar that ʿUmar ibn al-Khaṭṭāb (may Allah be pleased with him) recited Sūrat al-Ḥajj and prostrated in it twice, then said: "Indeed this sūra has been favoured with two prostrations."

And with its isnād from Mālik from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Dīnār, that he said: "I saw ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar prostrate twice in al-Ḥajj."

And Aḫbaranā Abū Bakr al-Jawzaqī, who said: Aḫbaranā Abū al-ʿAbbās al-Daʿūlī, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ibn Abī Khaythama, who said: Ḥaddathanā Abū Salama al-Khuzāʿī Manṣūr ibn Salama, who said: Ḥaddathanā Ḥammād ibn Salama from ʿAlī ibn Zayd from Ṣafwān ibn Mihrān that Abū Mūsā recited Sūrat al-Ḥajj on the pulpit of Basra, then descended and prostrated in it twice.
